title: Sharing the Road with Driverless Cars

blanks.sentence: With a human driver, a person outside the car can make _____ to help decide who should move first.
One road user says he might feel a little _____ when crossing in front of a robotaxi.
Because accidents may happen when approaching danger is unseen, a researcher wants to improve driverless cars' _____.
blanks.section: Making the vehicles easier to notice

blanks.sentence: Two kinds of signals were tested: moving displays called _____ and a fixed light display.
blanks.section: Making the vehicles easier to notice

blanks.sentence: Runners and cyclists have _____ to decide what to do, so a quick look may miss a moving display.
blanks.section: Making the vehicles easier to notice

blanks.sentence: One example shows a _____ to indicate that crossing is safe.
blanks.section: Making the vehicles easier to notice

blanks.sentence: The team used _____ to warn faster-moving road users instead.
blanks.section: Making the vehicles easier to notice

blanks.sentence: In one culture, a wave of the hand can mean "_____", inviting another road user forward.

multipleChoice.question: What central difficulty arises when a driverless car meets someone outside it?
options: The car cannot identify the person's planned route.
The person lacks a human driver to signal who should move first.
The person cannot know who is riding inside the car.
The car cannot be seen by anyone on the road.

multipleChoice.question: How does one road user say he might respond to a robotaxi at a crossing?
options: He might let it pass and cross behind it.
He might signal for it to stop and cross first.
He might follow it to another road junction.
He might remain inside until it has passed.

multipleChoice.question: What change does one speaker cautiously expect as driverless cars become more familiar?
options: People may no longer need to choose when to cross.
People may learn to stop the cars whenever they wish.
People may better judge how and when to cross near them.
People may avoid all roads used by the cars.

multipleChoice.question: Why does a researcher want driverless cars to stand out more clearly?
options: Road users often disagree about hand gestures.
Cyclists may not follow the same legal rules.
Human drivers sometimes miss the pedestrians ahead.
Accidents may happen when approaching danger is unseen.

multipleChoice.question: Why did the moving displays work less well for runners and cyclists than for pedestrians?
options: The displays could only be seen at crossings.
Faster users might not take in an animation during a glance.
The images showed a message meant for cyclists only.
The displays changed meaning between different cultures.

multipleChoice.question: What does the hand-waving example show about road communication?
options: A gesture is clear only when it lasts a long time.
A gesture is understood identically in all countries.
The same gesture can carry different cultural meanings.
Hand movements are always clearer than light signals.

multipleChoice.question: How does the speaker contrast jaywalking in South Korea and the UK?
options: It is accepted in both places but less common in Korea.
It is common in Korea but rare in the UK.
It is illegal in the UK but accepted in Korea.
It is illegal in Korea but frequent in the UK.

multipleChoice.question: What broader point follows from the comparison of jaywalking habits?
options: Local road behaviour can affect conditions for autonomous cars.
Legal penalties alone decide whether autonomous cars are safe.
Autonomous cars are safe only where jaywalking is illegal.
Rare jaywalking removes the need for vehicle warning signals.
